justification: The counterexample is exactly the reference construction. All variables are bounded and integrable. Both one-step conditional-mean identities hold: averaging over the independent sign gives E[X_2|X_1]=X_1, and at X_2=0 the two possible X_3 values average to zero. Yet on {X_1=1,X_2=0}, with probability 1/4, E[X_3|F_2]=1≠0=X_2.
